headline: Wave 8 (after wave 7 merged): the collaboration module, the owner's status issue and the standard repository guide, as 16 areas in 8 groups (order below). Input: the collaboration audit of 2026-11-02 (four parts: a two-person walk with two daemons and two UIs on one Postgres, a code review with probes, a test review with a two-daemon bench, a design part; each checked by a skeptic who reproduced it on a bench of their own). All majors were confirmed; the module's tests pass (integration 66/66 and 73/73 with Postgres, unit 330/330, e2e 04, 08, 09) because every one seeds membership by hand in one process. Four root causes cover most findings: identity binds a store's only person to any new install; two membership lists disagree and most routes apply neither; a session is treated as dead when another computer runs it; desktops have no change feed or outbox. Same pipeline as phase E: failing test first at the person's boundary (two daemons driven through the UI's client, and the two-person bench journey), the full suite with FORERUNNER_TEST_PG at every stage, an independent reviewer who walks it on the two-person bench, one merge at a time. Read at 71c97cd (fix/decisions was being merged at the time; fix/verification unmerged).

areas.title: One task, one runner: another person's session is information on your PC and can never be stopped or paused from it; an agent that lost its claim stops at once and never moves or pushes the task; the running chip and Stop all count your own sessions only
problems: [major] (walk missed item, code C1, tests T-01; confirmed three times, on bench and probe) Stop now or Stop after this task pressed on the other person's live session marks it stopped, frees its claims and lets the same task run twice. POST /sessions/:id/stop (packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1569 at 71c97cd) and /pause (:1597) call endDeadSession whenever rt.kill.activeCount is 0 in this process, which is always so for a run on another PC; endDeadSession (packages/runtime/src/session/recovery.ts:76-131) releases the claims of row.agent_id (recovery.ts:118: the other person's agent) and sets the row stopped. Startup recovery is scoped to this install's device (recovery.ts:183), these routes are not. Bench (skeptic-tests probe2.out; skeptic-walk evidence.txt): Bob's POST /sessions/<Ada's running session>/stop answered 200 'Stopped by you. "Ada slow task 1…" is ready again.'; Bob's next session ran the same task while Ada's PC still finished it; two coder runs for one task; Ada's row ends 'stopped' with two session.ended events. The UI path is the running chip or 'Open running session' to SessionPage, whose Stop buttons show for any running session (apps/ui/src/pages/SessionPage.tsx:306, :321). Introduced this round by the dead-session path (86c1e27).

[major] (code C3, design collab-04; confirmed; C3's 'the PR ends up with whichever push came last' is overstated per its verdict) An agent that loses its claim during a run does not notice. The renewal error is swallowed (runner.ts:1442 `void store.task.renewClaim(...).catch(() => undefined)`), the task watch compares the status only (runner.ts:2727 `row.status !== "in_progress"`), and TaskRepo.transition checks the version, never the holder (packages/state/src/repos/task.ts:225-258), while expireClaims at the other PC's session start (runner.ts:902; task.ts:199-206) frees a lapsed in_progress claim. Bench (skeptic-design, Ada's daemon suspended by PID with SIGSTOP, then resumed): Ada's resumed run moved the task Bob held to in_review under her agent while claimed_by was Bob's agent; her critic accepted it; both runs spent money. The other run's watch usually stops within taskWatchMs (5 s, runner.ts:595) and a late push without force is refused, so the harm is the duplicate spend, the wrong owner and words that quote the other agent's summary as if a person moved the task.

[major] (walk C-07, tests T-09; confirmed) The running chip, Stop all and the project page count the other person's sessions. workingOn (packages/runtime/src/daemon/project-status.ts:333-366) takes the newest planned, running or paused session on the project whatever its agent; the card's action is 'Open running session' (project-status.ts:178), which replaces Start; ShellBars.tsx:19-22 counts every working card; POST /kill (server.ts:1634) stops only this process. While only Ada's PC worked, Bob's header read 'Alice is working on "Check that…" · Stop all (1 running)' and his project page offered no Start (walk steps/bob/11, 19; tests bench bob/steps/04).

[minor] (design skeptic missed item; confirmed on bench) POST /sessions (server.ts:1394) passes body.agentId to the scheduler and runner.start loads that agent without checking whose it is: Bob's daemon ran a session as Ada's agent, with cost rows on Ada's monthly cap and Bob's billing source. The UI always sends its own agent (StartSessionDialog.tsx:258, ShellBars.tsx:175), so only an API caller reaches it today.

Pinned while fewer than three issues are pinned, else left unpinned and Settings says so. (2) One comment per writer (GitHub login + install device id + principal agent), created once and then only edited in place: '<!-- forerunner:status-writer v1 key=K install=<device> agent=<agent id> -->', '**Ada's agent (Forerunner)** · ada-gh · updated 2 Nov 21:05 UTC', 'Working on now' lines '- Add a footer · branch fr/… · files footer.html · since 21:00 · until 22:30 UTC', 'Waiting for Merge' '- #12 Write notes page', and 'Last session (2 Nov 20:59 UTC): did 1 task: "Write notes page". Next: "Add styles".' Never in a comment or the body: costs, chat words, Inbox answers, email addresses, secrets or @mentions (a mention notifies). (3) The body is a view rebuilt from all writers' comments, so a lost body write loses nothing: 'Each person and agent keeps one comment below up to date; this summary is rebuilt from them. How to work here: AGENTS.md.'; Summary (goal, what is done lately, next); Working on now (every fresh line, whose; then 'Not seen since' for expired ones); Waiting for Merge; Latest (one line per writer); 'Rebuilt <time> from N comments'. Rewritten after each session (debounced 30 s; re-read and rebuilt at most twice when a comment changed after the snapshot). (4) When the writer's comment changes: task start (a line, until = now + 90 min), every 30 minutes while the task runs (until renewed), task end (line removed; an accepted PR goes to Waiting for Merge; a merged one disappears), session end (Last session, then the body), Quit (lines cleared, best effort); only by the task's claim holder. Writes are coalesced (one pending text per writer and issue, kept in the store for this install, sent when GitHub answers); reads use the ETag. (5) Tampering and loss: my comment is known by its stored id, my login and my marker; edited by someone else → restored and my person told once; deleted → recreated; a comment by another login carrying my marker is treated as theirs; an issue a person closed is not reopened ('The status issue #12 was closed on GitHub; reopen it there to use it again.'); a deleted issue gets one new issue and the person is told once. (6) When GitHub cannot be written, the status stays in the app with one sentence in the Docs tab and the project's Settings: issues off: 'Status stays in the app: issues are turned off on owner/repo.'; no permission: 'Status stays in the app: Forerunner may not write issues on owner/repo (the GitHub key needs Issues: read and write).'; offline, a GitHub error or the rate limit: 'Status on GitHub: last updated 14:05; it updates when GitHub answers.'; pin refused: the issue works unpinned. (7) The project's Settings: 'Status on GitHub: issue #12 (pinned)' with an off switch, and on a public repository 'Everyone who can see this repository can read it.'; the Docs tab: 'In the app; also on GitHub: issue #12'; the guide ('repo-guide') gets the issue number as a fact.
